question: In the banking package (Capital Requirements Regulation III), the co-legislators tasked the Commission with monitoring the implementation of international standards in the area of market risk. They also empowered the Commission to adopt a delegated act to adapt the Union framework in the event that differences are identified (Capital Requirements Regulation, Article 461a).

The differences in both the final UK standards and in the proposed US standards implementing the final Basel III package can already be anticipated. How is the Commission planning to ensure a level playing field for trading in financial instruments?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (22.3.2024) In the United States (US), the public consultation on the proposed standards to implement Basel III finished in January 2024. So far, US agencies have indicated that they intend to finalise the rules in the summer, but the Federal Reserve Chair recently said that he expects that there will be ‘broad and material changes’ to the proposed standards.

The United Kingdom published its ‘near final’ rules for market risk in December 2023, but has not yet completed the implementation for other parts, such as credit risk (the announced date of application is 1 July 2025). Given the importance of having an international level playing field, the Commission is closely monitoring the implementation of the Basel III international standards in other major jurisdictions.
The empowerment referred to by the Honourable Member ensures that the Commission can take action if needed.
